_meta.description: Phase 0 eval set for validation-plan-staged-pipeline.md. 25 Airbnb-style rental-marketplace component needs across four categories (search_discovery, listing_detail, booking_checkout, host_guest_account), each with a hand-written gold answer: expected verdict and an 8-item requirements checklist, same rigor as the project's original 5 hand-validated cases.
_meta.gold_authoring_note: Gold verdicts are this author's expert judgment of what a careful manual search of shadcn/ui and 21st.dev SHOULD find, not a guarantee of what a live web_search call will actually surface. They exist as a fixed comparison target for Phase 3, not as a claim of ground truth about the live component ecosystem at query time.
_meta.existing_cases_note: 5 of the 25 (ids: price-breakdown, cancellation-policy, host-earnings-dashboard, image-gallery, host-guest-messaging) are the project's original hand-validated cases from PRODUCT_BRIEF.md. Their gold verdicts are reused as-is rather than re-derived, except where this project's own later live testing (documented in README.md) established a more reliable finding than the original by-hand guess -- see per-case notes.
_meta.tightening_pass_note: Revised 2026-08-26 after Phase 2's smoke test on date-range-picker showed the original gold (use_existing, 100%) was too generous: a real staged-pipeline run against shadcn's actual official range-picker pattern found it genuinely doesn't include separate labeled check-in/check-out fields, a nights/price display, or a reset control, landing at 3/8 (37.5%), custom_build, unanimous across a 3-run ensemble. That's not a pipeline defect -- it's evidence the initial gold answer was graded on 'a plausible pattern exists' rather than checking every specific requirement against real capability. Before Phase 3, re-reviewed all 25 gold answers against a fresh, independent extraction cross-check (eval/gold-tightening-extraction.json) with that same stricter standard. 21 of 25 held up -- several (price-breakdown, host-earnings-dashboard, guest-count-selector) converged almost exactly with the independent extraction, reinforcing confidence in those. 4 were revised: date-range-picker (verdict flipped to custom_build, now backed by real live evidence rather than a guess), availability-calendar and notification-preferences (coverage/confidence lowered -- both had 1-2 gold items that looked plausible for a 'simple' need but aren't actually bundled into the generic component), and filter-panel (coverage lowered similarly). See each revised case's rationale for specifics.

cases.component_need: search results grid with map toggle

gold.rationale: A synced list/map split view tied to real geocoded listings is a compound, domain-specific pattern. Generic libraries don't ship a listing-grid-plus-synced-map component; at best a generic card grid and a bare map embed exist separately, uncombined.

requirements.requirement: Toggle or split view between grid and map
Listing cards showing photo, price/night, and rating
Map pins synced to the currently visible listings
Hovering a pin highlights the corresponding card
Infinite scroll or pagination through results
Map collapses or hides on mobile viewports
Loading skeleton state for the grid

cases.component_need: filter panel for price, amenities, and property type

gold.rationale: Tightened in the post-Phase-2 revision pass. Faceted filter sidebars (price range slider, checkbox lists, category select) are a common ecommerce pattern, but the original 75% estimate assumed the whole checklist was 'generic enough' without checking each item individually -- collapsible per-group sections and a mobile bottom-sheet variant are real UI-kit features, not guaranteed to ship with a bare filter-panel component the way the core slider/checkbox/apply/clear elements are.

requirements.requirement: Property type select or radio group
Active filter count badge on the trigger
Mobile: filters open in a bottom sheet/drawer

cases.component_need: location, date, and guest search bar with autocomplete

gold.rationale: The three-segment merged pill (where/when/who) with per-segment expanding popovers is Airbnb's own signature pattern. The underlying primitives (combobox, date range, stepper) exist individually, but the compound assembly does not.

requirements.requirement: Check-in/check-out date range picker inline in the bar
Guest count stepper covering adults, children, infants, pets
Three segments visually merged into a single pill control
Active segment expands into a popover/dropdown
Mobile: full-screen modal instead of inline popovers

cases.component_need: sort control for search results by price, rating, and distance

gold.rationale: A labeled dropdown with a fixed option list and a selected-state indicator is a standard select/dropdown-menu pattern, fully covered by generic libraries.

requirements.requirement: Dropdown trigger showing the current sort option
List of sort options (price low-high, high-low, rating, distance)
Compact trigger style matching a results toolbar

cases.component_need: saved listings / wishlist grid

gold.rationale: A card grid with a favorite/heart toggle is a common ecommerce wishlist pattern. Airbnb's named-collection grouping is the one piece generic components won't have.

requirements.requirement: Grid layout of saved item cards
Heart/save toggle icon on each card
Empty state when nothing is saved
Card shows image, price, and rating
Click-through to the listing detail page

cases.component_need: image gallery for a property listing

gold.coverage_estimate: genuinely boundary -- do not treat a single verdict as fixed ground truth for this case
gold.rationale: PRODUCT_BRIEF.md's original by-hand validation called this a clean 100% commodity match. This project's own later live testing (see README.md, Ensemble cost section) found the opposite in practice: this specific case kept flipping between use_existing and custom_build across outer runs even with the ensemble active, always landing on a 2/3 split with confidence low. That documented instability is preserved here on purpose -- this is the one case in the eval set that exists specifically to test whether a staged pipeline reduces run-to-run variance on a genuinely ambiguous input, not to assert a single correct answer.

requirements.requirement: Category tabs within the gallery (bedroom, kitchen, etc.)

cases.component_need: amenities list with icons

gold.rationale: An icon-plus-label grid with a show-more expansion is a simple, common composition pattern well within reach of generic component blocks.

requirements.requirement: Grid of amenity items, each icon plus label
"Show all N amenities" expand or modal
Icons for common amenities (wifi, kitchen, parking, pool)
Unavailable amenities shown struck-through or hidden
Search/filter within the full amenities modal

cases.component_need: host profile card with superhost badge and response rate

gold.rationale: A generic avatar+card component covers the layout shell, but the Superhost badge system, response-rate/response-time stats, and hosting-tenure fields are platform-specific data points no generic component ships with.

requirements.requirement: Response rate and response time stats
Number of reviews and overall rating
Link to the full host profile page

cases.component_need: reviews list with rating breakdown

gold.rationale: Star-rated review cards are common, but the multi-category sub-rating breakdown (cleanliness, communication, accuracy, etc.) and per-star distribution histogram are specific enough that generic components only cover the list half of this need.

requirements.requirement: Overall star rating and review count header
Category sub-rating bars (cleanliness, accuracy, communication, etc.)
Individual review cards with avatar, name, date
Host response shown inline under a review

cases.component_need: interactive neighborhood map on the listing page

gold.rationale: Real map integration plus domain-specific content (privacy-blurred pin, walk score, nearby POIs) is not something generic UI libraries provide -- this needs an actual mapping SDK, not just a styled component.

requirements.requirement: Embedded interactive map centered on the listing

cases.component_need: availability calendar showing booked and open dates

gold.rationale: Tightened in the post-Phase-2 revision pass using real evidence: the date-range-picker case's actual staged-pipeline run found shadcn/ui's real Calendar (react-day-picker) natively supports disabled-date logic, multi-month display, and keyboard nav, but nothing about a legend or price-per-night overlay came up in that grounded search evidence -- both were originally marked met on assumption, not evidence. Corrected here; still use_existing since the core calendar mechanics are a strong match, but confidence drops from high to low now that coverage sits in the 40-79% band instead of >=80%.

requirements.requirement: Visually distinct styling for booked vs. available dates

cases.component_need: price breakdown with fees and taxes

gold.rationale: Reuses the project's own canonical case. Multiple live runs this session (see scripts/verify-memory*.mjs logs) landed consistently in the 2/8-3/8 range across different phrasings of this need -- more heavily evidenced than a single by-hand guess, used here as gold in preference to the original product-brief figure.

cases.component_need: cancellation policy display

gold.rationale: Reuses the project's original hand-validated finding: no real candidate exists for a tiered, date-threshold refund policy display. Kept as reason no_candidates_found rather than a scored low-coverage result, per the project's own distinction between the two.

requirements.requirement: Timeline/date markers showing when the refund amount changes
"Learn more" link to full policy details

cases.component_need: date range picker for check-in and check-out

gold.rationale: Replaced with a real finding, not a guess -- this is the case that triggered the whole gold-tightening pass. A live staged-pipeline run (Phase 2 smoke test) searched and found shadcn/ui's actual official range date-picker pattern (Popover + Calendar, built on react-day-picker): it natively handles dual-month display, range selection with highlighting, disabled-date logic, and min/max range length via props. But the grounded search evidence explicitly stated it does NOT natively include separate labeled 'Check-in'/'Check-out' trigger fields (just one combined Popover trigger), a nights-count/price display, or a reset button -- those need custom work on top. Scored 3/8 (37.5%) and confirmed custom_build unanimously across a 3-run boundary-risk ensemble. The original 100%/textbook-match gold was wrong: 'shadcn has range-mode calendars' is true but doesn't mean every specific requirement is met out of the box.

requirements.requirement: Two distinct, clearly labeled 'Check-in'/'Check-out' triggers that open a calendar
Calendar view (dual-month) letting user pick start then end date to form contiguous range
Booked/unavailable dates from listing availability visibly disabled
Past dates disabled and check-out constrained after check-in
Selected range visually highlighted across days in between
Clear/reset control plus keyboard navigation and aria labels

cases.component_need: guest count selector with adults, children, infants, and pets

gold.rationale: The stepper mechanics are generic, but the occupancy-cap rules (infants excluded from the cap, pets flagged separately, per-category descriptions) are domain-specific policy logic that generic components don't encode.

requirements.requirement: Separate steppers for adults, children, infants, pets
Infants/pets excluded from the guest-cap count
Popover/dropdown trigger showing the current summary

cases.component_need: payment method entry form

gold.rationale: Card entry forms are one of the most commodified checkout patterns in existence; extensive coverage in both shadcn-derived form kits and 21st.dev checkout blocks.

requirements.requirement: Billing address fields or reuse-existing-address toggle

cases.component_need: booking confirmation summary screen

gold.rationale: Order-confirmation summary blocks are common in ecommerce checkout kits; rental-specific fields (check-in instructions, host contact) are the gap.

requirements.requirement: Listing thumbnail, title, and host name

cases.component_need: promo/coupon code input

gold.rationale: One of the most standardized ecommerce checkout patterns; nothing rental-specific about it.

requirements.requirement: Success state showing the discount applied
Applied code shown as a removable chip
Discount amount reflected in the price summary
Disabled input state while a code is already applied

cases.component_need: host earnings dashboard

gold.rationale: Reuses the project's original hand-validated finding (71%, low confidence, 'partial match with real gaps'). A control-test run this session (see scripts/verify-memory-control.mjs output) landed at 2/8 for a stricter requirement set, so this case's exact coverage is sensitive to how the requirements are extracted -- a good candidate to watch in Phase 1's consistency check.

requirements.requirement: Summary cards for total gross/net earnings by period
Table of individual payouts/transactions with date, amount, status
Date-range picker to select the earnings period
Breakdown of earnings by individual listing

cases.component_need: host-guest messaging inbox

gold.rationale: Reuses the project's original hand-validated finding: shadcn/ui's June 2026 chat primitives turned this from a likely custom build into a near-perfect match (documented in README.md, No caching by design). The one case in the original 5 whose gold answer changed because the real ecosystem shipped new components -- a live reminder that gold answers here are snapshots, same as any recommend_component call.

requirements.requirement: Conversation list sidebar with unread indicators
Message thread view with sender avatars
Reservation context card pinned above the thread

cases.component_need: guest trip itinerary / upcoming reservations list

gold.rationale: Trip-centric grouping tied to real bookings, with rental-specific fields (check-in instructions, confirmation codes, countdowns), is not a generic component pattern.

requirements.requirement: List/cards of upcoming trips grouped by date
Each card shows listing photo, dates, and host name
Past trips section separate from upcoming
Countdown to check-in ("Trip starts in 3 days")

cases.component_need: host multi-listing management table

gold.rationale: A sortable/filterable data table with row actions is exactly what shadcn's Data Table (TanStack) is built for; only the domain-specific status/performance columns are a gap.

requirements.requirement: Search bar to filter by listing name

cases.component_need: host calendar sync and availability management

gold.rationale: The calendar grid itself is well covered, but multi-platform iCal sync status, per-date pricing overrides, and minimum-stay rule editing are backend-integration-heavy features no UI component ships with.

requirements.requirement: Calendar grid showing availability status per date
Sync status indicators for connected external calendars
Minimum-stay rule editor per date range

cases.component_need: guest reservation details / manage booking screen

gold.rationale: Overlaps heavily with booking-confirmation, but adds modify/cancel actions and policy-warning states that push it toward the boundary -- a deliberately close-to-threshold case for the eval set.

requirements.requirement: Total paid and payment method on file

cases.component_need: notification preferences settings panel

gold.rationale: Tightened in the post-Phase-2 revision pass. Grouped toggle-list settings panels are genuinely generic and common, but 100% assumed every listed item ships with a bare toggle-list component. The independent extraction cross-check (eval/gold-tightening-extraction.json) produced its own checklist for this need without seeing mine, and notably never included a digest-frequency selector or an unsaved-changes navigation guard -- both are real, but less-common additions on top of a basic toggle list, not part of the base pattern.
